text:
The issue seems to be in lines 32-33: `elif len(current) + 1 + len(word) < width:`.
This condition checks if adding the next word (plus a space) is *strictly less than* the width.
If the total length is exactly equal to the width, it incorrectly starts a new line (lines 34-36).
To fix this, I should change the condition to `len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= width`.

I will use `edit_file` to make this change.

text:
The tests passed. I can now submit the changes.
The bug was that the `wrap` function incorrectly started a new line when the total length of the current line plus the next word was exactly equal to the specified width. This was due to a strict less than comparison (`<`) instead of a less than or equal to comparison (`<=`). I have corrected this by changing the condition on line 33 of `wrapper/wrap.py` from `< width` to `<= width`. This ensures that lines that exactly fit the specified width are not unnecessarily wrapped, resolving the issue where lines were one character short. The tests have been run and passed, confirming the fix.
